paper.title: Online Learning for Multi-Layer Hierarchical Inference under Partial and Policy-Dependent Feedback

settings.name_in_paper: Online routing for multi-layer hierarchical inference under long-term resource constraints and terminal-only feedback
unmapped: Multi-layer hierarchical routing: each node's loss is defined recursively via downstream routing decisions
Terminal-only, policy-dependent feedback: a job's loss is observed only if it reaches the oracle layer, with probability depending on downstream policies
Experts are threshold-destination pairs over a confidence score; regret is per node and per task type
Job arrivals are i.i.d. over time slots with bounded first and second moments
Long-term resource constraints are handled through Lyapunov virtual queues; periodic model placement under memory constraints
settings.definition_quote: We study online routing for multi-layer hierarchical inference under long-term resource constraints and terminal-only feedback. ... Feedback is revealed only if a job is routed to the oracle layer; as a result, the probability of observing loss at a node depends recursively on downstream routing decisions under the global policy.

symbols.N_exp: |E_n(y)| = |H_y||U_n|, number of joint threshold-destination experts at node n for task type y
symbols.V_sum: sum over jobs j of E[1{y(j)=y} 1{n in path} V_{n,y}(j)], where V_{n,y}(j) is the weighted second moment plus the max squared value of the variance-reduced loss estimates

conditions: Assumption 3.1 (i.i.d. stationary arrivals with bounded first and second moments)
the proof assumes eta * F_max < 1, where F_max bounds the shifted loss estimates

source.label: theorem:regret
source.quote: For $\eta > 0$, the expected node-level regret $R_{n,y}(\Gamma)$ relative to the best fixed threshold-destination pair $(h^*, n'^{*}) \in \mathcal{E}_n(y)$ is strictly bounded by R_{n,y}(\Gamma) \le \frac{\ln(|\mathcal{E}_n(y)|)}{\eta} + \eta \sum_{j=1}^\Gamma \mathbb{E}[ \mathbbm{1}_{y(j)=y} \mathbbm{1}_{n \in \Omega^{\boldsymbol{\pi},j}} V_{n,y}(j) ]

results.notes: The horizon is Gamma jobs, not T slots. The bound depends on the data through a variance proxy. With eta proportional to 1/sqrt(Gamma) the paper claims O(sqrt(Gamma)). Regret is measured on per-node Lyapunov-weighted losses. 'Expected regret' is defined through expectations of per-job losses.

symbols.alpha_ly: Lyapunov drift constant bounding the per-slot squared cost deviation
symbols.Psi_max: uniform upper bound on the expected variance proxy
symbols.E_max: maximum cardinality of the joint expert space
symbols.eps_0: discretization error of the expert threshold grid

conditions: the best fixed discretized policy satisfies the resource constraints

source.label: cor:optimality
source.quote: By setting the learning rate to $\eta = \sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{Y}| \ln |\mathcal{E}_{max}|}{\Gamma \Psi_{max}}}$, the optimality gap of the proposed VR-Ly-EXP4 algorithm is strictly bounded by: $$\Phi_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{\pi}) - \Phi_\Gamma(\boldsymbol{\pi}^*) \le \frac{\alpha}{v \bar{A}} + \frac{2 |\mathcal{N}|}{v} \sqrt{\frac{|\mathcal{Y}| \Psi_{max} \ln|\mathcal{E}_{max}|}{\Gamma}} + \varepsilon_0$$

results.notes: This bounds the time-averaged system inference error gap (per job) against the optimal continuous policy, not a cumulative regret. Multiplying by Gamma would give the total gap. The learning rate needs Gamma and Psi_max. The proof uses N for the number of intermediate nodes.
